newsitem.title: USA: CBOT AUGUST SOYBEANS END SHARPLY HIGHER ON SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: CBOT AUGUST SOYBEANS END SHARPLY HIGHER ON SUPPLY.

text.p: Tightening near-term supplies of U.S. soybeans pushed CBOT August soybean futures sky-high on the close Wednesday, while other months ended with only modest gains, traders and analysts said.

"I think we're finally reaching the bottom of the bin," said Daniel Basse, grain analyst with AgResource in Chicago. "We may not have (new crop) beans available until the first or second week in October."
There is talk that soybeans are needed to meet export commitments on the U.S. Great Lakes and the Gulf of Mexico, but supplies of old crop soybeans are not adequate.
Last week's soybean export sales were healthy and seen as a sign that world demand is shifting from South America to the United States, Basse said.
One exporter in northern Ohio said 90,000 tonnes of soybeans would be needed to meet export commitments for the first half of September, but supplies are scarce.
CIF values for soybeans at the U.S. Gulf for delivery during first half of September rose 10 cents per bushel on Wednesday, cash sources said.
CBOT soybeans ended 1-1/2 to 35-1/4 cents per bushel higher. August settled up 35-1/4 cents at $7.79 per bushel.
Gains in new-crop months were limited by favorable growing weather throughout much of the U.S. Midwest and the prospects for a large crop this fall, traders and analysts said.

On Tuesday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast a record soybean crop of 2.744 million bushels. That figure was up 15 percent from last year's crop and higher than trade expectations for 2.607 billion to 2.731 billion bushels.
CBOT traders also said the market's ability to hold key support seen at $6.05 per bushel in November was also a factor in the market's rebound.
On the day, Merrill Lynch bought 1.5 million bushels November and Cargill and Goldenberg Hehmeyer each bought one million November. Tenco sold one million November, pit traders said.
In options trade, Smith Barney sold 1,000 November $6.50 calls, Cargill Investor Services sold 300 November $7.00 calls and L.B. Stern sold 200 November $6.50 calls.
Volatility was estimated at 20-3/4 percent in November, and September was pegged at 29 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 46,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 48,185.
